about: workflow:read-my-notices: reads the newest notices Trillion told the person (optionally of one kind), with the place each was seen, how far each way got and why a way did not carry it, read straight from the person's own store in the store's own language (rule a-tool-is-only-what-the-store-cannot-do). It replaces tool:my-notices in tools/tell-the-person, which listed the told-the-person records through the retired records door. Nothing here writes a notice: a notice is written by the one that tells it.

payload.label: Read my notices
payload.job: Read the newest notices told to the person, optionally of one kind, with whether each was read and acted on, read straight from the person's own store: the notices table every notice is kept in and the person's devices read.
payload.produces: A newest-first list of the person's notices, each with its id, kind, title, body, link, when it was made and whether it was read, read from the store's notices table.

source.from: tools/tell-the-person read-data/told.mjs (myNotices, keptNotices) and tool:my-notices, read on trillion-workshop origin/main 75fa3807fc
source.note: Only the reading is the store's job. Every notice is one row of the store's notices table (with devices, the table the device, mark-read and act-on-a-notice workflows use), so the read is the store's own query. The retired records door that listed the told-the-person records is not carried, and neither is the per-channel told and why view: delivery is the devices' route now.

where.description: Where the person keeps these things: the store's own address

language.description: How that store is spoken to, in its own terms

credential_name.description: The vault name of the login the run uses, when it needs one

kind.description: Only notices of this kind, applied before the newest are taken

limit.description: How many of the newest notices to show (default 20)

steps.title: Read what the store already keeps
steps.do: Speak to the store in its own language, with the login under its credential_name, and read its own description of what it holds. Submit whether it keeps a notices table (kept_in: its name, or null when none is kept yet) and the names of the objects that already keep notices and devices.

steps.title: Make the store's notice objects, once
steps.do: Make the store's notice objects where any is missing, in its own language (PostgreSQL), with these three statements in order through tool:run-sql-in-my-database, each of which changes nothing when its object is already there: (1) create table if not exists devices (id text primary key, platform text not null check (platform in ('live', 'web-push', 'apns')), token text, app_build text, registered_at timestamptz not null default now(), last_seen_at timestamptz not null default now()); (2) create table if not exists notices (id bigint generated always as identity primary key, device_id text references devices (id), title text not null default '', body text not null default '', url text, made_at timestamptz not null default now(), read_at timestamptz, acted_at timestamptz); (3) alter table notices add column if not exists kind text, add column if not exists key text. Nothing else is written here. Submit the names of the objects the store now has for notices.

steps.title: Prove the view on the example notices
steps.do: In a throwaway schema of the same store, with the same three statements, keep these four example notices in order (each insert into notices (title, body, url, kind) with made_at as given): 1 {kind: "take-me-there", title: "Notice 1", made_at: "2026-01-01T00:01:00Z", url: "https://example.test/1", read_at: "2026-01-01T00:05:00Z"}; 2 {kind: "report", title: "Notice 2", made_at: "2026-01-01T00:02:00Z"}; 3 {kind: "report", title: "Notice 3", made_at: "2026-01-01T00:03:00Z"}; 4 {kind: "report", title: "Notice 4", body: "The short body", made_at: "2026-01-01T00:04:00Z"}. Then answer three reads, each from those notices only. (1) Read with limit 2 and no kind: told:4 then told:3; told:4 has body "The short body", url null, read false; said "2 notices, newest first; 0 seen.". (2) Read with kind take-me-there: only told:1, url "https://example.test/1", read true; said "1 notice, newest first; 1 seen.". (3) Read with no notices kept: notices [], said "0 notices, newest first; 0 seen.". Then remove the throwaway schema. Submit answers: one per read, in order, exactly as above.

steps.title: Read the notices the person was told
steps.do: Read the store's notices: select id, kind, title, body, url, made_at, read_at, acted_at from notices, where kind = input.kind when input.kind is given, newest id first, the first input.limit (default 20, at most 100). For each row answer: id "told:<id>" (the id the mark-read and act-on-a-notice workflows take); kind (or null); title; body; url (or null); at (made_at as an ISO time); read (true when read_at is set); read_at and acted_at when set. Then say "<n> notice or notices, newest first; <s> seen.", where n is how many were shown and s is how many of those were read ("notice" when n is 1, "notices" otherwise). Answer {notices, said}. Nothing is written.
